enso.impact: Warmer, drier winters with less mountain snow. That points at a lighter snowpack feeding next spring’s irrigation, an earlier and warmer spring, and a longer, drier late summer at the farm.

plain.title: El Niño is building
plain.define: El Niño means the tropical Pacific Ocean is running warmer than normal. Once it holds more than about half a degree above normal, it counts as El Niño — and that tends to make our winters milder and drier with less mountain snow.
plain.timing: It usually strengthens through fall and peaks in the heart of winter (November–January), so the biggest effects here land December–March. You have the summer and fall before it really shows up.
plain.rate: The ocean has swung about 1.5°C warmer over the last six months — a fast move.
